intro: Learn to describe your daily morning routine and how often you do things.
b1.texto:
To talk about regular days we use the plural article: **los lunes**, **los sábados**.
Adverbs of frequency tell us how regular something is:
- **siempre**
- **a veces**
- **nunca** (before the verb it needs no 'no': *Nunca me levanto temprano*).

With **yo**, many routine verbs take the reflexive pronoun **me**: *me levanto, me ducho, me visto*.
b4.texto: Compare things you do every day with weekend activities.
b6.pregunta: On which day do people usually sleep longer?
b6.o0.refuerzo: Exactly! At the weekend people rest more.
b6.o1.refuerzo: Monday is when the working week begins.
b6.o2.refuerzo: Usually people do sleep more on Saturdays.
b7.o0.refuerzo: Correct! Me levanto temprano describes getting out of bed.
b7.o1.refuerzo: Sleeping early does not fit the idea of getting up.
b7.o2.refuerzo: Having breakfast early is not the usual expression here.
b8.traduccion: On Saturdays I sleep more hours.
b9.pregunta: Translate into Spanish: «I get up at seven.»
p.el lunes.consejo: The first working day of the week.
p.el sábado.consejo: The first day of the weekend.
p.siempre.consejo: At every moment, or with constant regularity.
p.a veces.consejo: On some occasions, but not always.
p.me levanto.consejo: The action of leaving your bed.
p.temprano.consejo: In the first hours of the morning.
p.duermo.consejo: First person of the irregular verb «dormir»: «o» becomes «ue».
p.me ducho.consejo: Washing yourself under the shower water.
b2.f0.texto: I get up at seven in the morning.
b2.f2.texto: On Saturdays I sleep more in my bed.
b2.f3.texto: Sometimes I have breakfast at home, without hurrying.
b2.f4.texto: I always shower with hot water.
b2.f5.texto: Then I get dressed quickly to go out.
b4.e0.texto: On Mondays I get up at seven.
b4.e1.texto: She never has breakfast in bed.
b5.f0.texto: My alarm goes off very early in the morning on Mondays.
b5.f1.texto: I get up at seven o'clock sharp and go straight to the bathroom.
b5.f2.texto: There I shower with scented soap and put on comfortable work clothes.
b5.f3.texto: In the kitchen I have coffee with milk and two slices of toast with sweet jam.
b5.f4.texto: My daily routine changes completely at the weekend.
b5.f5.texto: I sleep many more hours and never leave the house before noon.
b7.frase: Yo nunca ___ temprano por la mañana.
p.sábados.consejo: The accent mark falls on the first syllable: «SA-ba-dos». Days of the week are written in lowercase in Spanish.
p.cama.consejo: Say a hard «k» at the start: «KA-ma». It is the same «c» as in «casa».
p.lunes.consejo: Singular and plural look the same: «el lunes», «los lunes». Only the little word before it changes.
p.desayuna.consejo: From «desayunar»: «des-» plus «ayuno» (fasting). You literally break the fast each morning.
p.alarma.consejo: Stress the middle syllable: «a-LAR-ma». It is a feminine word: «la alarma».
p.punto.consejo: After a time, «en punto» means exactly on the hour: «las siete en punto» is seven o'clock sharp.
p.cuarto.consejo: «Cuarto» also means quarter or fourth, but here it is a room: «cuarto de baño».
p.baño.consejo: The «ñ» sounds like «ny»: «BA-nyo». It is also in «bañarse», to take a bath.
p.jabón.consejo: The «j» sounds like an «h»: «ha-BON». The accent mark shows the stress is on the last syllable.
p.aromático.consejo: The tilde marks the stress: «a-ro-MA-ti-ko». It belongs to the family of «aroma».
p.ropa.consejo: Roll the first «r» strongly: «RRO-pa». In Spanish «la ropa» is singular and means all your clothes.
p.cómoda.consejo: The tilde falls on the first syllable: «KO-mo-da». The masculine form is «cómodo».
p.tostadas.consejo: From «tostar», to toast. One slice is «una tostada»; two slices are «dos tostadas».
p.mermelada.consejo: Stress the third syllable: «mer-me-LA-da». It is the sweet fruit spread you put on toast.
p.rutina.consejo: The first «r» is strong: «rru-TI-na». It looks like the English word, but the stress is on «TI».
p.diaria.consejo: It comes from «día». «Rutina diaria» uses the feminine form because «rutina» is feminine.
p.completa.consejo: Stress «PLE»: «kom-PLE-ta». Feminine, to agree with «forma»; the masculine is «completo».
p.horas.consejo: The «h» is silent: «O-ras». It is the plural of «hora».
p.caliente.consejo: The «ie» is one sound: «ka-LYEN-te». It is the same for masculine and feminine, and related to «calor».
p.dulce.consejo: In Spain the «c» before «e» sounds like «th»: «DUL-the». It is the same for masculine and feminine.
